# NumCases dynamic helper and array ownership

MathJax CasesMethods.NumCases eventually parses its saved left expression plus
`\empheqlbrace\,` in a fresh TexParser with the caller environment and shared
command configuration. D2 does not enable Empheq's public configuration, but a
supported `DeclareMathOperator` or `DeclarePairedDelimiter` declaration can
provide that helper. The previous hardcoded undefined-helper failure ignored
those declarations, including declarations made inside the saved left program.

The fix implements the actual EqnArray owner and Cases.Entry second-column
scanner before invoking the existing Empheq layout helper. It preserves raw
command argument ownership, pending stack-item boundaries, internal text math,
row tags, initial-operator repair, spacing and late helper lookup. Cases.Entry
checks the current NumCases item before pushing its cell; a pending function,
style, position, Nonscript or group therefore must not trigger text scanning.
The second column trims only leading JavaScript whitespace and stops at the
source row/end/label tokens. Its scanner differs from ordinary `cases`.

The left child runs after closing the array and restoring the CasesBegin
lexical environment. It preserves fonts, multi-letter identifier rules, color,
style, vector state and root-index state while starting a new macro budget.
Body cells retain their independent empty lexical environments. Ninety-six
fresh original observations confirm the child environments and zero starting
macro count; every observed SVG equals the corresponding uninstrumented
original. The 96 observations and matching original SVG hashes are saved in
`numcases_child_environment_proof.json` and regenerated by the same original-only
generator, which verifies them against the complete SVG references. The
MathFont and OperatorName controls would lose source identifier state through the older conditional-copy parseArgumentString path.

## Original references

Current source base: actual main165 `5fd30978e6a93afce774885b2bf669caf8f4fe99`.
All 954 baseline and candidate outputs are byte-unchanged from the reviewed
main164 pair. The production patch rebases without conflicts or semantic
changes, confirmed by its identical stable Git patch ID.
Pinned original: MathJax `ad8f5c21cb810236551da8c6512ba733e67357ee`, using the
hash-verified frozen D2 assets and its fixed NoTags configuration. This change
does not enable Empheq macros or automatic CasesTags numbering globally.

The 954 distinct TeX/display pairs retain every original result:

- 902 strict complete-SVG assertions: all 764 valid original renderings and
  138 error renderings. There are 786 fixes and 116 unchanged exact controls.
- 52 raw outcomes: 50 original runtime exceptions and two original error SVGs.
  Forty-six empty-table inputs fail in original EmpheqUtil.left before a first
  mtd exists; Go returns a bounded nonnil conversion error, tested separately
  as an API boundary, not a passing original SVG. Four original NEL argument
  conversions fail at runtime and remain raw. The two body999 counter controls
  expose the inherited missing matched-end environment-budget charge; they are
  retained as wrong acceptance, not described as valid renderings.

The inventory combines the 700 author/source-scope controls, 112 independent
controls, 96 shared EqnArray row-item controls and 46 distinct previously
published diagnostic/runtime inputs.
Independent review's first incorrect display-mode capture is preserved in the
audit but expressly excluded; its corrected 112 originals are all exact.
No SVG geometry, diagnostics or attributes are normalized. No Go output is
used as an expected original result.

The actual main165 overlap scan reads all 430 tracked testdata JSON files.
Among the 902 strict input pairs, 893 are first input publications, eight
promote previously raw complete originals, and one was previously recorded
only as an augmented-package MML input. That last fixture declares display
mode globally, so its mode is resolved rather than counting it as a new input.
Its package contract differs from frozen D2 and no comparable old SVG exists.
All eight comparable original SVGs agree. These are per-fix input counts, not
a claim of globally unique coverage. Full identities are retained in the
inventory file.

The 5,802-input main165 published-raw replay finds eight genuine diagnostic
fixes and 38 changed original runtime failures that now return bounded errors.
One apparent cancellation regression is attribute-order variation: both
binaries emit both orders across 64 repeats, and all 128 complete parsed XML
trees match the original. The 4,326 upstream replay has one attribute-order-only
change to the already divergent `enclose` output: 128 repeated complete XML
trees match the unchanged baseline, but do not match the original's
undefined-package error. No original parity is claimed for that unrelated
helper. Both serialization observations are excluded from behavioral counts.
All other upstream outputs are byte-unchanged. Previous main164 receipts and
all raw original results remain preserved.

## Reproduction

```sh
node --jitless testdata/generate_numcases_dynamic_helper.cjs PINNED_ASSETS
go test -run 'TestNumCases' .
```

The generator verifies all frozen asset hashes and uses fresh original VMs.
It regenerates only original outputs; baseline/candidate receipts and the
passing/raw classification are not selected or rewritten by the generator.
All three original fixture files regenerate byte-identically on the complete
954-input inventory, including the 96 unmodified environment observations.
The actual main164 focused 902 complete-SVG / 46 bounded-runtime assertions,
full frozen-oracle suite, race checks, vet and WASM build passed serially with
Go 1.27 and `-p 1` at `9b72fc1cf7983a8955ebf1748bdb1aaa7c2a590a`.
On actual main165, the fresh probe, focused references, full frozen-oracle
suite, race checks, vet and WASM build all pass serially with `-p 1`. The
complete original inventory regenerates byte-identically. Final gates ran at
`e566ff4be3f2c4c6c184d8174d3ceb6e40ee9fe1`; the subsequent change only records
this verification in this README.
